title: Can Online Connections Match Offline Friendship
paragraphs: Many young people today spend a lot of time talking to friends online. But can online friendships be as good as friendships in the real world? Research suggests that the answer is not simple.

One study from 2023 looked at teenagers' friendships. It found that offline friendships were better overall than online friendships. However, online friendships had a higher level of intimacy. This means that people often shared more personal things with their online friends.

A newer study, published in the journal Computers in Human Behavior in 2026, followed 1,211 students in the Netherlands aged 10 to 15 for three years. The researchers, led by Federica Angelini of the University of Padova in Italy, found four types of social media users.

About 54% of the students used social media in a moderate way. They mainly used it to stay in touch with friends they also saw in person, and their friendships stayed good. About 30% rarely used social media, and they had weaker friendships at the start of the study. About 8% often shared their feelings online. They had more anxiety and depression, but they still had close friendships. Finally, about 7% mainly posted about themselves to get attention. This was the only group whose friendships became weaker over time.

According to the researchers, social media mostly made existing friendships stronger or weaker. Teens with good friendships in real life used it to keep those friendships. However, teens with weak friendships did not seem to benefit, because it was hard to build new friendships online. However, the study had limitations. The students reported their own behavior, and the study did not clearly separate friends met online from friends met in person.
Other research on adults has found that people with more online contacts who they had never met in person tended to be lonelier. However, it is not clear which causes which.
